clue.text: Thoughtless and really friendless girl

indicators.note: friendless means without an ally, so a word for friend is taken out of really

parts.note: miss is an unmarried girl or young woman

explanation.surface: Someone thoughtless who is also a lonely young woman with no friends at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'friendless' removes ALLY (a friend) from REALLY, leaving RE, which then takes MISS.
explanation.definitionFit: Remiss means negligent or careless of duty, close to thoughtless.

clue.text: He takes note of people's comings and goings

definitions.text: He takes note of people's comings and goings

parts.words: He takes note of people's comings and goings
parts.note: sounds like a doorman logging visitors, but means an official recording births and deaths

explanation.surface: A doorman or receptionist logging arrivals and departures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comings and goings' are births and deaths, which this official records.
explanation.definitionFit: A local official records births, marriages and deaths in the civil register.

clue.text: Frightened to do repairs without one

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word goes round another

parts.note: to mend is to do repairs
an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Scared of fixing things without help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as 'lacking', but here it has its old sense of 'outside': the repair word goes round the card word.
explanation.definitionFit: Menaced means threatened, so put in fear.

clue.text: Men putting the squeeze on foreigners carrying cash

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: strangers are outsiders or foreigners
L stands for pound (libra), a unit of money

explanation.surface: Locals pressuring visitors who are carrying money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting the squeeze on' sounds like extortion, but means literally throttling.
explanation.definitionFit: Throttlers choke victims by squeezing the throat.

clue.text: Getting very heated in a wet sort of way

definitions.text: Getting very heated in a wet sort of way

parts.words: Getting very heated in a wet sort of way
parts.note: sounds like losing one's temper, but describes burning with hot liquid or steam rather than with dry heat

explanation.surface: Someone flaring up in a tearful, overwrought manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting very heated' suggests anger; the wet heat is boiling water or steam, which burns in its own way.
explanation.definitionFit: To burn skin with boiling liquid or steam is to injure it this way, hence wet heat.

clue.text: Nothing is in short measure in this area

indicators.note: nothing is in, meaning it sits inside the next word

parts.note: curt means brief or short
O, the figure zero, means nothing
a yard is a measure of length

explanation.surface: In this zone nothing appears in small quantities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short measure' looks like one idea (giving too little) but is CURT and YARD.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclosed open space surrounded by buildings, a kind of area.

clue.text: See inside the joint

parts.note: lo means look or see
in means inside

explanation.surface: Look within the cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut of meat from an animal's back, such as pork or lamb.

clue.text: Subject to quarantine, also tie loosely

indicators.note: loosely means freely or not tightly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Keep someone confined and also bind them, though not tightly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loosely' rearranges ALSO and TIE.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate someone is to keep them apart, as in a medical quarantine.

clue.text: Precocious youngster making a thousand in profit

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: gain means profit
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A child prodigy earning a large sum.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamin is a street urchin, a cheeky, worldly child.

clue.text: Go downhill — no parking in overcrowded area of city

indicators.note: no parking means the letter for parking is dropped

parts.note: to slump is to decline sharply
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A city district declining, its streets so jammed there is nowhere to park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no parking' takes P out of SLUMP.
explanation.definitionFit: A slum is a squalid, crowded urban district.

clue.text: Military leader in overall …

definitions.meaning: a senior army officer of high rank
applying to the whole, not particular

explanation.surface: Military leader in overall …
explanation.definitionFit: A high-ranking army commander, and an adjective meaning broad or not specific.

clue.text: … even serving men wear it

definitions.meaning: soldiers and sailors in service wear standard dress

explanation.surface: A continuation: what serving men wear.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to 10 across, a general being a serving man; the two clues read as one sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Unvarying and constant, and the regulation outfit worn by service personnel.

clue.text: Inferior china for officer in Merchant Navy

parts.note: seconds are goods of inferior quality
rhyming slang: china plate means mate, a friend

explanation.surface: Cheap, flawed crockery being issued to a ship's officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'china' looks like crockery, matching 'Inferior' as seconds, but it is Cockney rhyming slang (china plate = mate).
explanation.definitionFit: A deck officer ranking just below the first mate on a merchant ship.

clue.text: Many a beard needs cutting frequently!

definitions.text: Many a beard needs cutting frequently!

parts.words: Many a beard needs cutting frequently!
parts.note: reads as a remark about facial hair, but describes a stretch of grass, which also grows and needs regular mowing

explanation.surface: A grumble that bearded men have to trim often.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'beard' is the grass growing on a garden plot, which must be mown regularly.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden area of short grass must be mown often, like a beard trimmed.

clue.text: Swallow grit and harm can result

parts.note: sand is grit
to mar is to damage or harm
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Gulping down grit could cause injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' is the bird, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The sand martin is a small bird of the swallow family that nests in sandbanks.

clue.text: Regiment did badly — arrived at front and was peppered with shot

parts.note: R is an abbreviation for regiment

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of did are jumbled

parts.note: to be the one arriving at the front is to have led

explanation.surface: A war report: a regiment fared poorly, reached the front line and came under fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' scrambles the clue's 'did'; 'arrived at front' means came first, i.e. took the lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Something riddled is perforated with many holes, as by gunfire.

clue.text: Dupe exceptionally nice man to get the upper hand

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat or dupe them

indicators.note: exceptionally means out of the ordinary, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Trick an unusually pleasant man to gain an advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exceptionally' rearranges NICE MAN into MINANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominance means control or superiority over others.

clue.text: A finish to the game the old city finds unprofessional

parts.note: mate (checkmate) ends a game of chess
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Someone from a historic town judges the end of a match to be poor sport.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'game' is chess, which ends in mate; UR is the ancient Sumerian city.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur plays for love rather than pay, so is not a professional.

clue.text: Thought to put spirit in a fellow

parts.note: rum is a spirit
in as written
Ted is a man's name, standing for any chap

explanation.surface: Someone thought of giving a man a stiff drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put spirit in' looks like an insertion, but here IN is just a piece in the charade.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruminate is to ponder at length, so ruminated means pondered.

clue.text: The beak making a stand

definitions.meaning: Latin ... is a bird's beak, and also a ship's prow
a raised platform for a speaker or conductor

explanation.surface: A magistrate rising to take a stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beak' is British slang for a magistrate, which suggests a courtroom, but here it is the bird's bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A rostrum is a bird's bill in zoology and also a speaker's platform.

clue.text: When there's drink left, keep up!

parts.note: to sup is to drink
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A drinker urged to keep pace while there's still some drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' is port, the left side of a ship, not 'remaining'.
explanation.definitionFit: To support is to hold up or bear the weight of.

clue.text: A revolutionary art movement — "Mad!" said models

indicators.note: to model is to shape or form, so these letters are moulded into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Critics call a radical art movement crazy, while those posing for its artists agree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'models' looks like the noun for artists' sitters, but it is a verb telling you to reshape MAD SAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Dada was an early twentieth-century anti-art movement that overturned artistic convention.

clue.text: Copy — trim it a teeny bit

indicators.note: a bit of the phrase gives the answer, so letters are taken from inside these words

explanation.surface: A request to trim something a tiny amount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a teeny bit' looks like a small amount; 'bit' signals letters lifted from TRIM IT A TEENY.
explanation.definitionFit: To imitate is to mimic or reproduce.

clue.text: The point about a work-out

parts.note: c (circa) means about, used with dates
PE, physical education, is a school exercise session

explanation.surface: The purpose of an exercise session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' is a headland here, not a purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: A headland jutting into the sea, such as a point on a coastline.

clue.text: Some American Indians quietly and stealthily advance

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people
p (piano) is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Native Americans moving in silently.
explanation.definitionFit: To creep is to move slowly and furtively.

clue.text: Hostelry getting enthusiastic reception, for modernisation

parts.note: an inn is a hostelry, a pub with rooms
an ovation is prolonged applause

explanation.surface: A pub's makeover is cheered for bringing it up to date.
explanation.definitionFit: Introducing new methods or ideas is a way of updating things.

clue.text: Too superior

explanation.definitionFit: Over means excessively as a prefix, and above in rank, as a boss over staff.

clue.text: Excellent form of punishment

explanation.surface: Praise for a good penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine means first-rate, and a sum of money paid as a penalty.

clue.text: Back no one so concerned with eating

indicators.note: back tells us the whole string of pieces is read from right to left

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone backs nobody, being so wrapped up in food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns the whole run NOISORE around.
explanation.definitionFit: Erosion is a wearing or gnawing away, as water eats into rock.

clue.text: Remove superfluous weight

parts.note: extra means more than needed
ct is the abbreviation for carat, a jeweller's weight

explanation.surface: A dieter told to shed surplus pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remove superfluous weight' reads like slimming advice; CT is the carat, used for gems.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract is to pull out or take away, as a dentist does a tooth.

clue.text: Beast gets in through someone dawdling about

indicators.note: the beast gets in, meaning it goes inside the word for through

parts.note: per means by way of or through
an otter is a river animal

explanation.surface: An animal getting inside thanks to an idler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'through' is not a signal here but supplies the Latin-derived word that holds the animal, which 'gets in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A potterer idles about doing small, aimless tasks without hurry.

clue.text: Absolutely denied involvement

indicators.note: involvement suggests letters wound up and twisted together into a new order

explanation.surface: Flatly rejected having any part in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involvement' rearranges DENIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are emphatic affirmatives, as in 'yes, certainly'.
